principles.rule: Prioritize conceptual integrity: every solution follows one clear design concept. Prefer consistency over feature count or cleverness.
checks: a single guiding concept stated before implementation

principles.rule: Design iteratively, not waterfall. Build the simplest working version first, then refine; let goals and solution co-evolve.
checks: no big up-front spec frozen before any build

principles.rule: Be empirical: validate assumptions with prototypes and tests rather than trusting correctness-by-reasoning.
Make user/usage assumptions explicit ('better wrong than vague') so they can be reviewed and corrected.
Treat constraints as friends: use budgets and limits (time, memory, interfaces) to shrink the solution space and focus the design.
Exercise requirements discipline: actively resist scope creep ('requirements sin'); more requirements rarely means a better product.
Invest care in the few bold, high-leverage design decisions; they account for most of the outcome's quality.
principles.source: The Design of Design, Preface, Case Studies
checks: key architectural decisions identified and deliberated
